title: ramp-constrained fleet autoscaler + 95p utilization sampler for safer burst expansion
author: Lina Ortega
release_notes: Introduce ramp-constrained autoscaler with per-pool ramp caps and a 95th-percentile utilization sampler. Improves stability during rapid traffic growth by limiting scale-up velocity and surfacing utilization regressions to the console. No config-breaking defaults; opt-in via feature flag.
description: Context: recent incidents showed large sudden spikes cause aggressive scale-ups that briefly oversubscribe neighbor pools and violate throughput guarantees for long-running tenants. This PR implements a safer autoscaling path that constrains ramp-up velocity at the FleetController level, surfaces a 95th-percentile utilization sampler for latency/throughput driven decisions, and adds telemetry for warm-pool and burst-usage so SRE can audit oversubscriptions. Changes include a new RampPolicy, a UtilizationSampler service, controller integration, feature flag gating, unit+integration tests, and console metrics wiring. The description below lists design highlights, rollout plan, and checklist. Design highlights: 1) RampPolicy: per-pool/time-window max-slot-add rate (slots/min) and a fractional headroom cap to avoid sudden pressure on shared NICs and scheduler. 2) SoftBurstSmoother: when a tenant's short-term demand suggests a burst, we now attach a transient smoothing lease (soft grant) that can be reclaimed without eviction; this preserves throughput guarantees for committed tenants while absorbing microbursts. 3) UtilizationSampler: lightweight sampler that computes 95th-percentile utilization per-pool over sliding windows (configurable: default 5m/60s buckets) and exports percentiles to the telemetry pipeline and the console. 4) Metrics: new metrics redwood_autoscaler_ramp_events_total, redwood_util_sampler_95p, redwood_softburst_reclaims_total, and per-pool labels for region/pool-type. Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag 'ramp-constrained-autoscaler' on prod; start in Canary pool for 48h with increased telemetry retention; enable in regional pools 7d after no regressions. Backout: set the feature flag to false to fall back to the legacy scaler, and a short-circuit for operators to forcibly drain smoothing leases. Checklist: - [x] RampPolicy core logic and unit tests - [x] UtilizationSampler implementation + histogram-backed tests - [x] Controller wiring and reconciliation tests - [x] Telemetry export + Influx/Tracing annotations - [x] Console dashboard stub for 95p and ramp events - [x] Feature flag and config docs - [x] E2E with small synthetic spike harness - [x] Rollout doc in docs/ops/ (linked) Related: ENG-3210 (predictable scale velocity), SUP-2043 (incident follow-up).

review_thread: Arjun Mehta: Please add a Prometheus label for pool_tier (critical/standard) so we can filter 95p by SLA tier. Also confirm cardinality implications.
Lina Ortega: Added pool_tier label to metrics and tested cardinality; sampler aggregates before export to keep cardinality bounded. See util_sampler.go#notes.
Becky Huang: Controller change looks good; can we ensure Reconcile path short-circuits if feature flag disabled to minimize added latency?
Lina Ortega: Reconcile now short-circuits early when the feature flag is off; added microbenchmarks to fleet_controller_test.go showing <200ns median overhead when disabled.
Mateo Ruiz: Integration tests failed initially on CI due to flakiness in the e2e harness (timing). Recommend a retry wrapper or increase tolerance.
Lina Ortega: Increased tolerances and added deterministic seed for synthetic load generator; CI re-run green.
SRE (comment): We need a runbook note for forced reclamation of smoothing leases; added ops docs and a CLI admin endpoint.
Security (automated): gosec static scan flagged a weak TLS fallback in telemetry exporter—addressed by tightening TLS config and pinning ciphers in internal/observability/telemetry_exporter.go.
Becky Huang: Approved after TLS change and added unit coverage. Arjun: Approved. Merge queued.
notes: Performance: microbenchmarks show ramp policy adds negligible controller latency when disabled and under 250us per Reconcile when enabled (mostly due to sampler calculation on heavy pools).
Ops: new dashboard linked in release notes; recommend 14d increased telemetry retention during Canary.
Config: default ramp cap is 10 slots/min per pool, configurable via charts/autoscaler/values.yaml.
Compatibility: backward compatible; feature disabled by default for existing clusters.
